subject: use recursive function in a model

messages.author: d128bd7b4bae8e43
messages.subject: use recursive function in a model
parts:
Hi,
I need a recursive function (to compute probabilities) and I've done it successfully. The function has a setup and it's actually its method that is recursive. It's as following :

f_gen <- nimbleFunction(
  setup(hyperParam){},
  run = function(some parameters){
    pini = ...
    p = Q(parameters)
    return(p)
    returnType(...)
  },
  methods = list(
    Q = function(parameters){
       ... Q() ...
    }
  )
)

f <- f_gen(hyper)
cf <- compileNimble(f)

f compiles and both : "f$run(parameters)"  and "cf$run(parameters)" give back the result.

My problem is that I need to use f in several samplers of my MCMC. I could just give the code in f and the method Q to all the samplers but I feel like there must be a better way.

Also, in "parameters" there are some of the model nodes, by giving the code of f to all the sampler I'd be able to directly use model$node instead of giving them as arguments of the function but is it possible to give the function a view of the model (as the sampler have) and use that function in other samplers ?

Regards,
Rémi

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: use recursive function in a model
parts:
Hi Rémi,

Yes, I think you can do what you want.

Define f_gen in the R global environment.  When you write a sampler that wants to use f_gen, include something like
f <- f_gen(hyper)
in the setup code of the sampler.  Then you can use f in the run code and methods.  They will be automatically compiled together.

In the format for writing a sampler, one of the arguments is the model.  If you add that as a setup argument to f_gen, which you will be calling from the sampler's setup code, then you can use it in the run code and methods of f_gen.  Again, the compiler will arrange for the compiled instances of f_get to use the compiled model.

Here is how you can get arbitrary information into the setup code of f_gen.  When you add a sampler to an MCMC configuration, the code looks like
MCMCconf$addSampler("target_node", my_new_sampler, ...) # (or you can use a control argument explicitly, instead of ...)
where entries in ... get put into the control list passed to the sampler's setup code.  You can make your sampler's setup code unpack named arguments from the control list and pass them to f_gen when you call it to create the instance f.

I hope that makes sense.

Perry
